findings.title: Device is cached before the DB write, so a rejected device is let through for 29 minutes
findings.body: tagDeviceUI marks the device key in localCache before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice. When the limit is reached, CreateOrUpdateDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, but the cache entry stays. Every later request from that device hits the early `localCache.Get` return and skips the DB check entirely, so Authenticate succeeds. The first request is rejected, and retries within the cache TTL are allowed. The device limit is therefore not enforced. The cache entry should be set only after a successful write, or removed when the write fails.

findings.title: Device limit check is a non-atomic count followed by insert
findings.body: CreateOrUpdateDevice counts devices and then inserts in separate statements with no transaction or lock. Concurrent first-time requests from distinct devices can all read a count below the limit and all insert, so the number of devices can exceed deviceLimit. The limit is only a soft bound under concurrency, which matters because the feature exists to cap devices.

findings.title: Anonymous login now does DB work synchronously on every request, without a timeout
findings.body: Authenticate previously ran TagDevice in a goroutine with a 2-minute timeout and a panic recover. Now it calls TagDevice inline with the request context. When deviceLimit is set, each anonymous request runs a COUNT query on anon_device, then an UPDATE or upsert, before authentication can complete. Slow DB latency now directly slows or fails every anonymous page load. The async behaviour and timeout were removed without a replacement.

findings.title: Runtime field typed as `undefined` instead of `number | undefined`
findings.body: `anonymousDeviceLimit = undefined;` gives the class property the literal type `undefined`, which contradicts the `number | undefined` declared in GrafanaConfig. Any code reading `config.anonymousDeviceLimit` through the class type will be treated as always undefined. It should be declared as `anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined = undefined;`.

findings.title: TypeScript type says the limit may be undefined, but the backend always sends a number
findings.body: The Go DTO field `AnonymousDeviceLimit` is `int64` without omitempty, so it is always serialized, defaulting to 0. The `number | undefined` type suggests the field may be absent, which the frontend never receives. The type should be `number`, with 0 meaning no limit documented.

findings.title: No tests for the existing-device update path or the anonymous login rejection path
findings.body: TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit covers only a new device being rejected at the limit. It does not check that an already-tagged device still updates when the limit is reached, which is the purpose of updateDevice. It also does not test that TagDevice or Authenticate returns the error, nor the cache bypass described above. The cache bypass in particular would have been caught by a test that repeats the rejected request.
